message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible public vulnerability reports and material advisory updates observed in the last 24 hours before the scheduled run on 2026-07-29 05:10 IST. Confirmed relevant updates were found for FortiOS, Ubuntu/Linux kernel, Samba, and NGINX.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Fortigate/FortiOS
- Issue: CVE-2025-68686, Fortinet FortiOS Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor Vulnerability
- Severity: Medium, based on Fortinet CNA CVSS 3.1 score 5.9. NVD had not provided its own CVSS assessment at review time.
- Description: FortiOS SSL-VPN may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass a patch for a symbolic-link persistence mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases via crafted HTTP requests. NVD notes that the attacker would first need filesystem-level compromise through another vulnerability.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Fortigate/FortiOS, and NVD explicitly lists affected FortiOS versions. The fresh development is CISA adding the vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-07-27, with NVD modified again on 2026-07-28.
- Source: NVD CVE-2025-68686 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-68686; Fortinet advisory referenced by NVD https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt/FG-IR-25-934

**Finding 2**

- Product: Ubuntu / Linux kernel
- Issue: Multiple Ubuntu Linux kernel vulnerability notices, including USN-8618-1, USN-8620-1, and USN-8574-3
- Severity: Not clearly stated as a single severity in the Ubuntu notices.
- Description: Ubuntu published multiple 2026-07-28 Linux kernel security notices covering many kernel subsystems and cloud/HWE kernel variants. The notices describe issues that could allow system compromise, information disclosure, or local privilege escalation depending on the affected CVE and kernel flavor.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and the notices explicitly apply to supported Ubuntu releases including 20.04 LTS, 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and/or 26.04 LTS depending on the notice.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8618-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8618-1; Ubuntu USN-8620-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8620-1; Ubuntu USN-8574-3 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8574-3

**Finding 3**

- Product: Samba / CIFS-SMB services
- Issue: USN-8621-1 and Debian DSA-6401-1 for Samba vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-6949, CVE-2026-58216, CVE-2026-58218, CVE-2026-58221, CVE-2026-58222, CVE-2026-58224, plus CVE-2026-15779 in Ubuntu
- Severity: Not clearly stated as a single severity in the Ubuntu or Debian advisory.
- Description: The Samba advisories cover denial of service, information disclosure, privilege escalation, and a more serious authenticated LDAP issue that could permit unauthorized modifications and domain control.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Samba and CIFS/SMB Utils. Ubuntu describes the package as an SMB/CIFS file, print, and login server for Unix, and Debian likewise identifies the affected package as Samba.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8621-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8621-1; Debian DSA-6401-1 https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00312.html

**Finding 4**

- Product: NGINX
- Issue: Existing NGINX CVEs with new July 28 exploit-development coverage: CVE-2026-42533, CVE-2026-60005, and CVE-2026-56434
- Severity: NGINX rates CVE-2026-42533 as major, CVE-2026-60005 as medium, and CVE-2026-56434 as medium.
- Description: NGINX 1.30.4 and 1.31.3 fixed a map/regex buffer overflow, a slice-module memory disclosure issue, and an SSI-module use-after-free. The vulnerabilities were originally patched on 2026-07-15, but public reporting on 2026-07-28 noted a full-chain proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-42533.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Nginx, and the official NGINX advisory page explicitly lists the affected NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus vulnerabilities. The fresh item is exploit-development/public PoC coverage, not the original disclosure date.
- Source: NGINX advisories https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html; NGINX 2026 news https://nginx.org/2026.html; The Hacker News update https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-nginx-vulnerability-can-crash.html

**Possible matches needing review**

- Microsoft Edge: Microsoft published a 2026-07-27 Edge for Android and iOS security release that incorporates Chromium security updates, but the page did not list specific CVEs for that entry. Treat as an update candidate for mobile Edge fleets, not a fully detailed vulnerability finding. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security
- WordPress plugin reports: A new 2026-07-28 Wordfence entry for Cost Calculator Builder PRO was excluded from confirmed findings because Products.txt lists WordPress, Yoast SEO, and Advanced Custom Fields, but not that third-party plugin.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for FortiOS because CISA now lists CVE-2025-68686 as known exploited, and for NGINX deployments still below 1.30.4 or 1.31.3 because public exploit details are now circulating. Ubuntu kernel and Samba updates should be reviewed through the normal Linux patch process.
